versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10825 (24 FR 4825, PDF pages 1-3; Federal Register issue of June 13, 1959; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10825.txt), headed Executive Order 10825, signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower on June 12, 1959. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Excusing Federal Employees From Duty All Day on July 3, 1959). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: section 1(a) excuses covered employees from duty all day on Friday, July 3, 1959 (with section 1(b) giving a rule for employees whose workday spans two calendar days); section 2 limits the excusal for national-security employees and employees working or excused on Saturday, July 4, 1959; section 3 gives employees who are not excused on July 3, 1959 one other workday off in fiscal year 1960; section 4 denies any basis for holiday, premium or overtime pay for July 3, 1959 and requests agency heads to arrange their affairs for the excusal. Inventory correction: the dossier's second clause (subsection (b)) runs from section 1 across a Register page break and then through the Contents and unrelated Register documents. The order is split by a page break (continued on next page), and the last sentence of section 4 is badly damaged in the text layer; I use five spans: section 1, section 2, section 3, the first part of section 4, and the surviving fragment of the end of section 4. The recitals are not operative and are not clauses. The damaged fragment is read against the American Presidency Project transcription (not quoted, and not cited as a source), which shows that the last sentence of section 4 requests agency heads to arrange their affairs so that employees can be excused from duty on that day or given compensatory time, without additional appropriations. Own terms: sections 1, 2 and 4 are tied to July 3 and 4, 1959; section 3 runs to the end of fiscal year 1960, which is June 30, 1960 (the Government's fiscal year ran from July 1 to June 30; that statutory definition is not a held text and the order does not state the date, so I disclose that the end of section 3 rests on it). The whole order therefore ends on June 30, 1960.
